newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria adopts new measures to spur non-oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Algeria adopts new measures to spur non-oil exports.

text.p: The Algerian government on Wednesday unveiled a wide-ranging strategy aimed at boosting non-oil and gas exports and diversifying the energy-dominated economy, the official Algerian news agency APS said.
The government forecast $2.0 billion non-oil and gas exports by the year 2000 compared to $538 million in 1996, and $350 million in 1995.

The government has set up the Algerian Office for Promotion of Foreign Trade (PROMEX), a fund and a credit insurance for exports through which the state will channel subsidies, and eased loans to help Algerian exporters, APS said.
The government will also streamline rules governing exports and exempt exporters from income and Value Added Tax, APS added.
Algeria's exports totalled about $13 billion in 1996 against roughly $10 billion in 1995, thanks to a surge in crude oil prices on the world market.
The government expects annual export receipts of $18 billion by the year 2000, due mostly to increased gas sales and a fourfold rise in non-oil and gas exports by 2000.
Algeria's main exports outside the oil sector are agricultural products, mostly wine and dates, and iron, steel and petrochemical goods.
